title: bee-core fsutil semantics + unknown-field round-trip property tests
action: Port fsutil semantics into bee-core (member scaffolded by rust-port-1): writeJsonAtomic (temp file + rename in same dir), appendJsonl fail-open, tolerant readJson/readJsonl including truncated-tail tolerance. ORACLE RULE (advisor note 5): 'matching the mjs reader' is proven by running the REAL mjs reader on the same corrupt fixtures (file-based node driver, never node -e) and diffing results against the rust reader — never by the worker's reading of fsutil.mjs alone. Serde discipline per D3: every store struct round-trips unknown fields (serde flatten capture) — property tests prove an mjs-written record with extra fields survives a rust read-modify-write byte-semantically (no field loss). Test names prefixed fsutil_ so the cell verify filter catches them.

truths: unknown JSON fields survive read-modify-write round-trips
atomic write leaves either the old or the new file content on simulated crash between temp-write and rename
truncated/corrupt jsonl fixtures produce identical results from the rust reader and the real mjs reader run on the same bytes

artifacts.substantive: fsutil module + property tests (fsutil_ prefixed) incl. mjs-oracle differ, no stubs

key_links: lock module (rust-port-3) consumes these primitives for lock body writes and contention.jsonl appends
oracle driver executes the real .bee/bin/lib/fsutil.mjs in a node child
prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/lib/fsutil.mjs (mjs frozen per D1)
No edits to crates/Cargo.toml (members final per rust-port-1)
Oracle tests never touch the repo's live .bee/ store

trace.outcome: Ported fsutil.mjs semantics into bee-core (ensure_dir, read_json, read_jsonl, write_json_atomic, append_jsonl) with an mjs-oracle differ proving parity against the real .bee/bin/lib/fsutil.mjs, red-first on the two behaviorally risky primitives (atomic write, corrupt-jsonl tolerance), plus a BOM/trim divergence the oracle caught and fixed.
